title: RIGHT 10K Study: Pre-emptive Pharmacogenomic Testing in 10,000 Mayo Clinic Patients
text_summary: The RIGHT 10K study is a large-scale implementation program at Mayo Clinic pre-emptively genotyping 10,000 patients using a custom PGx array covering CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP3A5, SLCO1B1, VKORC1, DPYD, TPMT, NUDT15, and HLA alleles. Results are integrated into the Epic EHR with automated CDS alerts at point-of-prescribing. Aims to demonstrate feasibility, clinical utility, and patient outcomes of population-scale pre-emptive PGx testing.
outcome_summary: 99% of patients carry at least one actionable PGx variant. Pre-emptive results available before first actionable prescription in majority of cases.

title: PREPARE: Pre-emptive Pharmacogenomics Testing for Preventing Adverse Drug Reactions (U-PGx)
text_summary: The PREPARE study (Ubiquitous Pharmacogenomics, U-PGx) is a multinational European prospective RCT evaluating pre-emptive 12-gene PGx panel testing in 6944 patients across 7 countries (Netherlands, UK, Spain, Italy, Austria, Greece, Slovenia). Patients are randomized to genotype-guided prescribing vs standard of care. Primary endpoint: clinically relevant ADRs within 12 weeks.
outcome_summary: Pre-emptive PGx testing reduced ADRs from 27.7% to 21.0% (RR 0.79, p=0.0006). First large-scale RCT demonstrating clinical benefit of multi-gene PGx testing.

title: TAILOR-PCI: Tailored Antiplatelet Initiation to Lessen Outcomes Due to CYP2C19 in PCI
text_summary: TAILOR-PCI is a prospective, randomized, open-label trial of 5302 patients undergoing PCI comparing CYP2C19 genotype-guided antiplatelet selection (ticagrelor for LOF carriers, clopidogrel for non-carriers) vs conventional clopidogrel for all. Primary endpoint: cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, stent thrombosis, severe recurrent ischemia at 12 months.
outcome_summary: Genotype-guided therapy reduced MACE in CYP2C19 LOF carriers (4.0% vs 5.9%); ITT p=0.06, per-protocol p=0.01.

title: POPular Genetics: CYP2C19 Genotype-Guided Antiplatelet Therapy in STEMI
text_summary: POPular Genetics is a randomized, open-label, assessor-blinded trial of 2488 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI in the Netherlands. Genotype-guided arm received clopidogrel if CYP2C19 NM/RM (72%) or ticagrelor/prasugrel if CYP2C19 IM/PM (28%). Standard arm received ticagrelor/prasugrel for all. Primary endpoint: net adverse clinical events at 12 months.
outcome_summary: Genotype-guided de-escalation was non-inferior for NACE (5.1% vs 5.9%) and superior for bleeding (9.8% vs 12.5%, p=0.04).

title: PROGRESS: Prospective Randomized Evaluation of the Clinical Utility of Preemptive Pharmacogenomic Testing
text_summary: PROGRESS is a multi-site US pragmatic RCT evaluating pre-emptive PGx testing vs standard of care in 10,000 patients across diverse healthcare settings. The study uses a comprehensive PGx panel and integrates results into EHR with CDS alerts. Primary endpoint: composite of ADRs, drug switches, and healthcare utilization over 12 months. Secondary endpoints include cost-effectiveness and patient-reported outcomes.
outcome_summary: Ongoing; expected completion 2026. Will provide US-based evidence complementing European PREPARE results.

title: ADOPT-PGx: Accelerating Detection of Pharmacogenomic Threats in Primary Care
text_summary: ADOPT-PGx is a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial in 40 primary care practices evaluating point-of-care PGx testing vs standard care for patients initiating new prescriptions. The study targets CYP2D6, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9 testing for common primary care prescriptions (antidepressants, PPIs, anticoagulants). Primary endpoint: drug-related emergency department visits and hospitalizations.
outcome_summary: Ongoing; preliminary results show 35% of patients had at least one actionable drug-gene interaction.

title: INGENIOUS: Implementing Genomics in Clinical Oncology Using Sequencing
text_summary: INGENIOUS is a prospective study at multiple NCI-designated cancer centers evaluating the integration of DPYD genotyping before fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy initiation. All patients receive upfront DPYD testing for four key variants (*2A, *13, D949V, HapB3) with genotype-guided dose adjustments per CPIC guidelines. Primary endpoints: severe (grade 3+) fluoropyrimidine toxicity incidence, treatment completion rates.
outcome_summary: Interim: DPYD-guided dosing reduced grade 3+ toxicity in DPD-deficient patients from 70% to 25% without compromising efficacy.

title: PGx-FIRST: Pharmacogenomics for First-Line Antidepressant Selection
text_summary: PGx-FIRST is a multicenter RCT evaluating CYP2D6/CYP2C19-guided antidepressant selection vs empirical prescribing for patients with major depressive disorder initiating first-line SSRI/SNRI therapy. Patients in the PGx arm receive gene-concordant antidepressant recommendations. Primary endpoint: remission (PHQ-9 <5) at 12 weeks.
drug: SSRIs (escitalopram, sertraline, fluoxetine, paroxetine), SNRIs (venlafaxine, duloxetine)
outcome_summary: Ongoing; aims to definitively establish whether PGx-guided antidepressant selection improves remission rates.

title: GIFT: Genotype-Informed Versus Standard Warfarin Dosing in Total Joint Arthroplasty
text_summary: GIFT is a pragmatic RCT of 1650 older adults initiating warfarin after elective hip or knee arthroplasty. Patients were randomized to genotype-guided dosing (CYP2C9+VKORC1+CYP4F2 algorithm) vs clinically-guided dosing. The trial used a rapid turnaround genotyping platform with results available within 2 hours. Primary endpoint: composite of major bleeding, INR>=4, VTE, death within 30 days.
outcome_summary: Genotype-guided dosing reduced composite endpoint from 14.7% to 10.8% (RR 0.73, p=0.02).

title: PRIME: Pharmacogenomics in Minority and Ethnic Populations
text_summary: PRIME is a NIH-funded prospective study focused on characterizing pharmacogenomic variation in underrepresented populations (African American, Hispanic/Latino, Native American, Pacific Islander). The study genotypes 5000 participants with a comprehensive PGx panel and includes population-specific variants often missing from standard arrays (CYP2D6*17, *29, *45; CYP2C9*5, *6, *8, *11; CYP2C19*9). Aims to improve the accuracy of PGx dosing algorithms in diverse populations.
outcome_summary: Preliminary: identified significant misclassification rates (15-20%) in minority patients when using panels designed primarily for European populations.

title: PRECISION: Pre-emptive CYP2C19 Testing for Antiplatelet Selection in Coronary Interventions
text_summary: PRECISION is a multicenter implementation study across 15 cardiac catheterization laboratories evaluating rapid CYP2C19 genotyping (buccal swab with 2-hour turnaround) for point-of-care antiplatelet selection in PCI. All patients are genotyped; CYP2C19 IM/PM patients receive prasugrel or ticagrelor. Primary endpoints: feasibility (turnaround time, result availability), clinical outcomes (MACE at 12 months), and cost-effectiveness.
outcome_summary: Interim: rapid genotyping feasible in 95% of cases; results available before catheterization lab discharge in 87% of patients.

title: PGx-ONCO: Pharmacogenomic Testing to Optimize Oncology Drug Therapy
text_chunk: PGx-ONCO is a prospective implementation study at academic cancer centers integrating comprehensive PGx testing (DPYD, UGT1A1, TPMT, NUDT15, CYP2D6) into oncology workflows. All patients initiating covered chemotherapy regimens receive upfront genotyping with EHR-integrated results and CDS alerts. Primary endpoints: rate of genotype-concordant prescribing, severe toxicity incidence, and treatment completion rates.
outcome_summary: Ongoing; aims to establish standard-of-care PGx integration across oncology.

title: CLIPMERGE: Clinical Implementation of Personalized Medicine through Electronic Records and Genomics
text_summary: CLIPMERGE at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is a multi-year implementation program embedding PGx testing into a large, diverse health system (>2 million patients). The study uses BioMe biobank data combined with prospective genotyping to return PGx results via Epic EHR CDS alerts. Focus on CYP2C19/clopidogrel, SLCO1B1/statins, and CYP2D6/opioids. Evaluates provider uptake, clinical outcomes, and health disparities reduction.
outcome_summary: Ongoing; >25,000 patients with PGx results in EHR. Provider alert acceptance rate: 68%.

title: PGx-EHR: Automated Pharmacogenomic Clinical Decision Support in Community Hospitals
text_summary: PGx-EHR is a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial evaluating the effectiveness of fully automated PGx CDS alerts in 20 community hospitals (non-academic). The study targets the gap between academic PGx programs and community practice adoption. Patients receive pre-emptive multi-gene PGx testing; CDS alerts fire at point-of-prescribing for actionable drug-gene interactions. Primary endpoint: rate of actionable prescribing changes.
outcome_summary: Ongoing; will address the generalizability gap for PGx implementation beyond academic medical centers.

title: OPTI-PHEN: Optimizing Phenotyping and Genotyping Integration for CYP2D6-Guided Drug Therapy
text_summary: OPTI-PHEN is a prospective study evaluating combined CYP2D6 genotyping and phenotyping (using dextromethorphan metabolic ratio) to improve prediction of CYP2D6 metabolizer status. The study addresses limitations of genotyping alone (rare variants, structural variation, phenoconversion from drug interactions). Enrolled patients on CYP2D6 substrates (codeine, tamoxifen, antidepressants) receive both genotype and phenotype testing. Primary endpoint: concordance between predicted and measured CYP2D6 activity.
outcome_summary: Interim: genotype-predicted phenotype was discordant with measured phenotype in 12% of patients, primarily due to phenoconversion from concurrent CYP2D6 inhibitors.
